(1) A witnessed record's `pin` is `Some(fact.pin.clone())`, and a Fact's pin is `format!("sha256:{}", sha256_hex(&hash_input))` over each pending extent entry's label + world_root + world_state + output (src/facts.rs:414-436) — a content fingerprint of the observation, not "the tree it stood in". (2) A claim's currently stated pin is the backticked token parsed out of prose by `find_stated_pin` — a short git hash such as `abc1234`/`deadbee` in the crate's own tests. A `sha256:`-prefixed observation fingerprint can never equal one, so "a comparison of that stored pin against the claim's currently stated pin, answerable on ledgers already written" would fire on every witnessed-grounded claim unconditionally rather than detecting a re-pin. The comparison the design wants is against `world`.     recs.append((s['name'],s['digest']['sha256'],pr['pass'],pr['verdict'],pr.get('timestamp')))

same=0; cross=0; disc=[]; ordinals=collections.Counter()
for k,g in pairs.items():
    seenpass=[]; seenverd=set()
    for i,r in enumerate(g):
        newws = r[2] not in seenpass
        if i>0:
            if newws: cross+=1
            else: same+=1
        if newws and i>0 and r[3] not in seenverd:
            ord_=len(seenpass)+1
            ordinals[ord_]+=1
            disc.append((k[0],r[2],sorted(seenverd),r[3],ord_))
        if newws: seenpass.append(r[2])
        seenverd.add(r[3])
print('same-workspace repeats',same,'cross-workspace repeats',cross)

ws=[len(set(x[2] for x in g)) for g in pairs.values()]
print('total workspace-gradings',sum(ws))
for N in (1,2,3,4):
    print('N=',N,'gradings',sum(min(N,w) for w in ws),'retained',sum(c for o,c in ordinals.items() if o<=N))

A clean-tree marker is sha256(commit_sha + NUL) — nothing else enters it — so it is reproducible by any pass at any future time that checks out that commit with a clean tracked tree. Computing that for all 89 reachable commits and matching against the frozen world_state in each memo's shipped facts.jsonl: all five memos' single authoring markers, tet28/29/30/46 included, are each the clean-tree marker of a still-reachable commit. So "it stops being dischargeable at the next commit, permanently" is wrong, and "the state four of the five memos in this repository are already in" is wrong about all four. What makes a marker unreproducible is the commit becoming unreachable, or the authoring tree having been dirty — neither of which is "the next commit", and neither of which is true of any memo here. The inference the claim draws from it ("an owed condition satisfiable only until the next commit and unsatisfiable forever after is not a schedule") therefore has no antecedent, and the reason given for excluding rule 3 from the owed predicate does not hold. This memo's own first sentence asserts the pinned commit can be re-opened and read as it was, which is the same capability the claim says a later pass does not have.

The claim's stated ground for preferring a report over a schedule is that "the divergence re-arms permanently at the next commit and a memo whose authoring tree was dirty can never be matched again at all". Measured: the divergence does not re-arm permanently — a clean-tree marker is sha256(commit_sha + NUL), so it is reproducible forever by a pass checking out that commit, and all five memos' authoring markers here are exactly that. And the dirty-tree escape is vacuous in this corpus: every one of the five memos was authored against a clean tree, so zero memos are in the state the claim relies on to make the divergence unclearable. What remains true is only the narrow half the claim already concedes — a pass standing at the pinned commit does reproduce the marker — which is an argument FOR schedulability, not against it. The remedy the claim recommends (carry `world` into EvidenceRecord and report) may still be right, but the reason given for it is refuted, and the design's own asymmetry between "report" and "schedule" turns entirely on that reason.
